items.technique: npm worm: harvest npm/cloud/SSH credentials at require time, then rewrite a writable package's scripts and bump version to propagate
items.what_the_real_incident_did: Shai-Hulud-style worm validated stolen npm tokens, enumerated writable packages, and republished each with a preinstall loader that re-ran the collector; the collector read ~/.npmrc, SSH keys and cloud credential files.
items.what_the_fixture_does: Collects ~/.npmrc, SSH and AWS files at require time and contains a propagate helper that sets scripts.preinstall and bumps the patch version, with transport and PUT stubbed out.

items.technique: setup.py cmdclass install override that downloads a Windows PE via PowerShell, adds a Defender exclusion and starts it
items.what_the_real_incident_did: MUT-8694 PyPI packages overrode install via cmdclass to fetch CBLines.exe with PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest, then ran it; the infostealer (Blank Grabber) added a Defender exclusion.
items.what_the_fixture_does: Overrides install in setup.py to fetch an executable with PowerShell, add a Defender exclusion path and call Start-Process, with the final execution step marked as never reached.

items.technique: CLI-invoked stealer that scans Discord LevelDB for tokens and lists Chromium/Edge cookie stores, then posts to a Discord webhook
items.what_the_real_incident_did: Skuld/Blank-Grabber-derived modules enumerated Discord token storage and browser cookie databases and exfiltrated results via a Discord webhook.
items.what_the_fixture_does: A devsync CLI subcommand scans Discord LevelDB for token patterns and lists browser cookie files, then builds a webhook payload that is not sent (placeholder URL).

items.technique: Git hooks and config in a zip-delivered repo: post-checkout/post-merge/pre-commit hooks, core.hooksPath, core.fsmonitor and a '!' alias that launch a downloader
items.what_the_real_incident_did: A recruiter 'take-home' zip contained .git/hooks scripts that ran on git checkout/pull/commit and downloaded OS-specific second-stage scripts in the background.
items.what_the_fixture_does: Hooks spawn a detached bootstrap that fetches an OS-specific stage script from a made-up CDN; .git/config sets hooksPath, an fsmonitor program and a shell alias.

items.technique: VS Code tasks.json runOn folderOpen plus Claude Code SessionStart hook that each launch a bootstrap script from the repo
items.what_the_real_incident_did: Shai-Hulud August 2026 committed .vscode/tasks.json with a folderOpen task and .claude/settings.json with a SessionStart hook, each running a setup.mjs that launched the worm.
items.what_the_fixture_does: Defines a folderOpen task and a SessionStart hook that run setup scripts; the setup script reads a list of credential paths (second stage not implemented).

items.technique: MCP tool whose description asks the model to attach SSH/AWS/npm credential files to the tool's result, returned to the model and client
items.what_the_real_incident_did: Invariant Labs' 2025 PoC poisoned a calculator tool description so the model read ~/.ssh keys and MCP config and passed them along during a normal call (described in the CSA note).
items.what_the_fixture_does: An MCP server whose read_project_file description instructs including credential files in the response, and whose handler reads those files into a _context field.

items.technique: .cursor/mcp.json with autoApprove wildcard, a shell-wrapped server command that fetches remote config, and an unrestricted shell bridge
items.what_the_real_incident_did: Project-level MCP configs in Cursor and similar IDEs auto-executed server commands with no per-run prompt; MCPoison (CVE-2025-54136) changed an approved server command with no re-approval.
items.what_the_fixture_does: Project mcp.json enables autoApprove for all tools, launches a shell command for a server, and points another server at an unrestricted shell bridge.

items.technique: Go module with a package init() that spawns cmd.exe on package load
items.what_the_real_incident_did: GHSA-22cv-9jv2-6m62 (gin-vue-admin, CVE-2026-48787) let an authenticated user inject Go source with func init() that ran os.StartProcess cmd.exe on rebuild; ATR documents the pattern.
items.what_the_fixture_does: A go-codegen library whose init() starts cmd.exe /c calc via exec.Command at package load, alongside a benign Generate function.

items.technique: Obfuscator-style hex string array with indirect index lookups; delayed 90s credential/env collection via setTimeout, unref'd
items.what_the_real_incident_did: Datadog found obfuscator.io-obfuscated npm index.js loaders; node-ipc 2026 appended an 80KB obfuscated payload that collected credentials and used a detached child process.
items.what_the_fixture_does: Looks like a retry library; hides path and method names in a hex array, collects dotfile credentials and env vars matching TOKEN/SECRET/KEY after a delay, and builds an unsent POST.

items.technique: postinstall script building PowerShell download/run commands from String.fromCharCode arrays and split literals on Windows
items.what_the_real_incident_did: The 'nodelogic' npm package used a postinstall hook to fetch CBLines.exe and LoPi.exe from GitHub with PowerShell and execute them, with payload strings obfuscated.
items.what_the_fixture_does: A postinstall on Windows builds an Invoke-WebRequest command from char codes and split strings to fetch two executables into the package folder, with launch step kept as text only.

items.technique: Python .pth persistence: a data-file .pth line imports a module that starts a delayed daemon thread checking a stage file
items.what_the_real_incident_did: MITRE documents Mini Shai-Hulud and TeamPCP using .pth import lines in site-packages to execute on every interpreter start.
items.what_the_fixture_does: Installs a clf_compat_init.pth whose import line arms a background thread that waits ten minutes before reading a staged file under the user cache directory; loader not implemented.

items.technique: Payload in a vendored sidecar file (vendor/cache.dat), XOR-decoded with a key from package.json config and written to tmp then required
items.what_the_real_incident_did: Compromised node-ipc versions appended an obfuscated payload that ran on require; Shai-Hulud copied the payload into package/math_init.js and wrote a loader beside it.
items.what_the_fixture_does: A socket helper that, when loaded, decodes a hex sidecar with a config-stored key, writes it to a temp .js file and requires it; the sidecar holds only a harmless placeholder string.

items.technique: Go init() schedules time.AfterFunc 15 minutes later that collects environment variables matching _TOKEN/_KEY/SECRET into a map
items.what_the_real_incident_did: ATR documents Go init() abuse for code execution; Datadog documents stealers that gather tokens after execution. Delayed collection in init is a variant described as a pattern, not a specific sample.
items.what_the_fixture_does: A secret-linter whose init() schedules a delayed collection of matching environment variables and a report function whose outbound POST is omitted.

items.technique: Agent skill whose helper reads ~/.claude.json and ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json, hex-encodes them and derives DNS-style labels, split across two scripts
items.what_the_real_incident_did: node-ipc 2026 targeted AI coding tool configs (.claude.json, .claude/mcp.json, .kiro/settings/mcp.json) in its credential sweep and exfiltrated them via DNS TXT queries.
items.what_the_fixture_does: A CSV-cleaning skill whose part1 module defines AI-tool config paths and part2 hex-encodes them into DNS-style labels for a lookup that is not issued.

items.technique: MCP server tool that rewrites ~/.cursor/mcp.json to add a new autoApprove server pointing to a local helper, path and key strings built from char codes
items.what_the_real_incident_did: CurXecute (CVE-2025-54135): a prompt injection via an approved MCP server made Cursor rewrite ~/.cursor/mcp.json to add an attacker-controlled server that auto-ran.
items.what_the_fixture_does: A lint MCP server whose lint tool re-writes ~/.cursor/mcp.json to register a sync helper with autoApprove '*', with the config filename assembled from char codes.

items.technique: VS Code folderOpen task (hidden dotfile script) plus task.allowAutomaticTasks on, loading a cached module from a hidden .cache directory
items.what_the_real_incident_did: Repo .vscode/tasks.json runOn folderOpen started setup scripts after the folder was opened, as in Shai-Hulud August 2026; dev.to notes the same autorun risk in take-home repos.
items.what_the_fixture_does: Settings allow automatic tasks; a folderOpen task runs a hidden prime script that lazily requires a cached module, which is a placeholder.

items.technique: GitHub Actions pull_request_target workflow that checks out the PR head with secrets in env and writes toJSON(secrets) to an artifact
items.what_the_real_incident_did: Shai-Hulud August 2026 injected a 'Run Copilot' workflow that wrote toJSON(secrets) into format-results.txt and downloaded it as an artifact. The spotipy advisory (title only read) describes secret exfiltration via pull_request_target.
items.what_the_fixture_does: A CI workflow on pull_request_target checks out untrusted PR head code, passes secrets to test env, and dumps toJSON(secrets) into an uploaded artifact via a format step.

items.technique: Clipboard watcher polling every 700 ms, matching cryptocurrency-address regex and replacing clipboard content with a reversed-literal destination
items.what_the_real_incident_did: Skuld Stealer's clipper module (described in Datadog MUT-8694) intercepted clipboard reads containing cryptocurrency wallet addresses and replaced them with attacker-controlled addresses.
items.what_the_fixture_does: An address-format library starts a clipboard watcher that matches an address regex and computes a replacement from a reversed placeholder; write-back is disabled.

items.technique: Base32-encoded credential files split into labels and DNS-resolved against a reversed zone name in a housekeeping call
items.what_the_real_incident_did: node-ipc 2026 exfiltrated gzipped archives as chunked, signed labels in DNS TXT queries to a look-alike domain.
items.what_the_fixture_does: A hardware-summary CLI whose helper base32-encodes ~/.gitconfig and ~/.netrc, chunks them into labels with a reversed zone, and builds (but does not issue) DNS queries.

items.technique: Skill instructs the agent to fetch remote instructions from a URL each run and says the remote document overrides the user's request, with conflicts not to be mentioned
items.what_the_real_incident_did: Mech.app describes repository files steering coding agents; CSA describes tool descriptions and files treated as authoritative instructions. Remote-instruction phrasing is a variant of this class.
items.what_the_fixture_does: A copywriting skill that tells the agent to fetch an external rules document each time, let it override the user's request, and keep conflicts hidden.

items.technique: AGENTS.md instructing the agent to add an autoApprove MCP server to .cursor/mcp.json and .mcp.json and install a global npm package without asking
items.what_the_real_incident_did: Forever Security (cited by mech.app) showed a malicious AGENTS.md prompting Codex to add an MCP server and install a malicious npm package in over 90% of runs.
items.what_the_fixture_does: AGENTS.md tells the agent to register an unpinned MCP helper with all tools auto-approved and to install a global package with no confirmation.

items.technique: CLAUDE.md instructing the agent to copy the AWS default profile including secret key into a repo fixture and commit it
items.what_the_real_incident_did: mech.app notes agents can be steered by repository files to exfiltrate credentials without a user prompt; the Forever Security CLAUDE.md variant redirected API traffic, showing CLAUDE.md is treated as policy.
items.what_the_fixture_does: CLAUDE.md tells the agent to copy ~/.aws/credentials default profile contents into a committed test fixture with a 'do not ignore' note.

items.technique: .cursorrules that pre-approves all MCP tool calls, hides arguments, pre-approves writes to home dotfiles and runs a publish with environment tokens on a trigger word
items.what_the_real_incident_did: CSA describes IDEs that auto-approved MCP servers and config changes; TrustFall showed folder trust prompts defaulting to yes. A rules file that pre-approves tool use is the instruction-level analogue.
items.what_the_fixture_does: A .cursorrules that removes confirmation for MCP calls and home-dotfile writes and runs release publishing on the word 'ship' using environment tokens.

items.technique: MCP server.json tool description with a plain-text 'Notes for the assistant' directive to read .env and pass it in an argument, with an instruction to omit this from the reply
items.what_the_real_incident_did: Invariant Labs' PoC (summarized in CSA) put exfiltration directives in a calculator tool description so the agent read SSH keys and sent them as parameters, silently.
items.what_the_fixture_does: A formatter tool manifest whose description asks the model to read and forward the project .env through an optional notes argument and not mention it.

items.technique: Skill tells the agent to pip install a helper wheel from an unfamiliar mirror URL and not switch to alternatives or verify hashes
items.what_the_real_incident_did: MUT-8694 PyPI packages used DLL/driver-repair and emulator-themed names to lure developers into installing packages that fetched infostealers.
items.what_the_fixture_does: A PDF-form skill whose setup installs a wheel from a non-index URL with a 'do not switch packages' note and advice to retry on hash mismatch.

items.technique: Take-home README instructing the candidate and their AI assistant to set core.hooksPath, accept VS Code automatic tasks, and return the zip including .git
items.what_the_real_incident_did: A recruiter 'take-home' zip with .git hooks was the delivery mechanism; dev.to notes the zip-with-.git delivery as the red flag, and that VS Code folderOpen tasks arrive via clone.
items.what_the_fixture_does: README tells the reader and their assistant to enable a hooks path, allow automatic tasks and send back a zip including .git, with the rest of the exercise innocuous.

items.technique: AGENTS.md instructing the agent to point scoped @acme packages and default registry at a made-up private registry via .npmrc and to retry 404s silently
items.what_the_real_incident_did: mech.app describes AGENTS.md steering installs; Shai-Hulud republished packages via npm registry PUTs, showing registry trust is a target. Registry redirection via agent instructions is a constructed variant.
items.what_the_fixture_does: AGENTS.md tells the agent to set the default and @acme registry to an unfamiliar host in .npmrc and to retry failed installs without reporting them.

notes: 27 fixtures: 8 plain, 11 obfuscated, 8 instruction-only (30/41/30 target). Actual type counts: config 7, npm-package 6, other 5, pypi-package 3, mcp 3, skill 3 (total 27). Each README is innocuous and names no attack hosts. Hosts are made up (.com/.net/.io, random-looking). Tokens and webhook IDs are PLACEHOLDER strings. Nothing is executed. Sources: fetched and read in substance: Datadog MUT-8694 (securitylabs.datadoghq.com), JFrog Shai-Hulud August 2026, SafeDep node-ipc analysis, MITRE ATT&CK T1546.018, ATR-2026-02194, dev.to cryptostrapon git hooks, dev.to mech.app indirect prompt injection, CSA MCP tool poisoning note. Secondary/partial: the CSA note and mech.app article are secondary syntheses; MITRE is a reference page; JFrog, SafeDep, Datadog are vendor research reporting on incidents (secondary to the incidents themselves). Partial only (headers/titles read, details not used): spotipy GHSA-h25v-8c87-rvm8 (title only, cited in item 17 for the title claim), StepSecurity Tensorlake (not cited for details), Mitiga, OX Security (HTTP 403, not read), Agimtula issue #21 (truncated, not cited), GuardDog PR 916 (truncated, not cited). Not sourced: DNS-exfil and .pth details beyond the cited sources; Gradle/Makefile and Ruby extconf were not covered (no fetched source). Dependency-confusion item 27 is a constructed variant of mech.app's AGENTS.md steering. Fixture 14 hex-label and 19 base32 DNS patterns are constructed from node-ipc's described exfil technique.
